questions.stem: Which of the following is a good sanitation practice in the home?
options: Sweeping the compound and clearing bushes around the house
Keeping refuse in open heaps near the kitchen
questions.explanation: Clearing bushes and keeping the compound clean removes hiding and breeding places for rats, snakes, flies and mosquitoes.

questions.stem: Monthly environmental sanitation exercises in Nigerian towns help mainly to
options: remove breeding places of flies, rats and mosquitoes
questions.explanation: Clearing drains, bushes and refuse during sanitation exercises removes places where disease carriers breed.

questions.stem: Which disease is most closely linked with poor disposal of human faeces and dirty drinking water?
questions.explanation: Cholera germs pass from faeces into water and food, so poor sanitation causes outbreaks; the other conditions are not spread this way.

questions.stem: A pit latrine should be sited well away from, and lower down the slope than, a well mainly to
options: reduce the cost of digging the well
make the latrine easier to find
prevent germs from the latrine from reaching the well water
questions.explanation: Water seeping from a latrine can carry germs through the soil; distance and siting it downhill protect the drinking water.

questions.stem: The food nutrient that mainly builds and repairs body tissues is
questions.explanation: Proteins from foods such as beans, fish, eggs and meat are used for growth and repair of tissues.

questions.stem: Which of the following foods is a good source of carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: Yam is a starchy food that gives energy; fish, egg and meat are mainly protein foods.

questions.stem: Lack of iodine in the diet can cause
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland; its lack causes the gland to swell, which is called goitre.

questions.stem: Bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds are signs of a lack of
questions.explanation: Vitamin C, found in oranges and fresh vegetables, prevents scurvy, whose signs include bleeding gums.

questions.stem: Roughage from fruits and vegetables is important in the diet because it
options: supplies most of the body's protein
questions.explanation: Roughage (fibre) adds bulk to food and helps it move through the intestines, preventing constipation.

questions.stem: A child who eats mainly cassava meals with very little protein for a long time is at risk of
questions.explanation: Cassava is rich in starch but very poor in protein, so a diet based on it alone can lead to kwashiorkor, a protein-deficiency disease.

questions.topic: Drug and substance abuse in the family
questions.stem: Which of the following could be a sign that a family member is abusing drugs?
options: Spending more time helping at home
Better results at school or work
Sudden change in behaviour, withdrawal and missing money at home
questions.explanation: Drug abuse often shows as mood changes, withdrawal from family, neglect of duties and stealing to buy drugs.

questions.topic: Drug and substance abuse in the family
questions.stem: A parent who smokes indoors harms the children mainly because they
options: breathe in second-hand smoke that damages the lungs
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoke in the home is breathed in by others and can cause coughs, asthma attacks and lung disease.

questions.topic: Drug and substance abuse in the family
questions.stem: Families can BEST help to prevent drug abuse among children by
options: keeping alcohol and cigarettes easy to reach
giving them money without asking how it is spent
talking openly with them, supervising them and setting good examples
questions.explanation: Good communication, supervision and positive role models help children make healthy choices and resist pressure.

questions.topic: Definition of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem: Air pollution is the
options: cooling of the air at night
movement of air from place to place
presence of harmful substances such as smoke and gases in the air
questions.explanation: Air is polluted when harmful materials such as smoke, dust and poisonous gases are added to it.

questions.topic: Definition of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem: Soil pollution is the
options: addition of harmful substances to the soil that make it unsafe or unproductive
questions.explanation: Soil becomes polluted when wastes, oil or excess chemicals harm the soil, its organisms and the crops grown on it.

questions.topic: Causes of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem: Which material is non-biodegradable and can pollute the soil for many years?
questions.explanation: Polythene is not broken down by micro-organisms, so it remains in the soil for a very long time.

questions.topic: Causes of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem: Burning refuse in the open mainly pollutes the
questions.explanation: Burning refuse releases smoke, soot and poisonous gases into the air.

questions.topic: Causes of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem: Spraying too much insecticide on farmland can pollute the soil by
options: killing useful soil organisms such as earthworms
increasing the number of soil organisms
making the soil darker and richer
questions.explanation: Excess insecticides harm earthworms and other organisms that keep the soil healthy.

questions.topic: Causes of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem: Excess fertilizer washed from farms into a pond causes rapid growth of algae. This harms fish mainly because the algae
options: provide too much food for the fish
use up the oxygen in the water when they die and decay
questions.explanation: The decay of the large mass of algae by bacteria uses up dissolved oxygen, so fish suffocate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a water-borne disease?
questions.explanation: Typhoid is spread by drinking water or eating food contaminated with germs from faeces.

questions.stem: Black soot in the air of some cities in the Niger Delta can cause
options: respiratory tract infections such as bronchitis
questions.explanation: Breathing in soot particles irritates and damages the airways and lungs.

questions.stem: Crops grown on soil polluted by crude oil usually
questions.explanation: Oil coats the soil, blocks air and water and poisons roots and soil organisms, so plants grow poorly.

questions.stem: Sulphur dioxide from burning fuels can dissolve in rain to form
options: acid rain that damages plants, buildings and water bodies
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water in the air to form acids, producing acid rain.

questions.stem: Continuous exposure to loud noise from generators and loudspeakers can lead to
questions.explanation: Noise pollution damages the ears over time and causes headaches, stress and poor sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following helps to reduce air pollution from vehicles?
options: Running engines when parked for long periods
questions.explanation: Well-serviced engines burn fuel more completely and give out less smoke and poisonous gas.

questions.stem: Industrial waste water should be treated before it is released into rivers in order to
options: remove harmful substances that could kill aquatic life and harm people
increase the colour of the river
add more chemicals to the river
questions.explanation: Treatment removes or neutralises poisons so the river remains safe for fish and for people downstream.

questions.stem: Burying refuse in a lined pit and covering each layer with soil is called
questions.explanation: A sanitary landfill keeps refuse covered and contained so it does not attract pests or pollute surrounding water.

questions.stem: The Nigerian agency set up to enforce environmental standards and regulations, including pollution control, is
questions.explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) enforces environmental laws in Nigeria.

questions.topic: Meaning, identification and classification of matter
questions.stem: Matter can be grouped into three states, namely
questions.explanation: All matter exists as a solid, a liquid or a gas.

questions.topic: Meaning, identification and classification of matter
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT matter?
questions.explanation: Light is a form of energy; it has no mass and does not occupy space, unlike air, water and sand.

questions.topic: Meaning, identification and classification of matter
questions.stem: Which of the following is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases such as nitrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide; oxygen and iron are elements and water is a compound.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Kerosene flows and takes the shape of its container, so it is a liquid.

questions.stem: The change of state from solid to liquid is called
questions.explanation: When a solid such as ice is heated, it melts into a liquid.

questions.stem: Naphthalene balls placed in a wardrobe get smaller over time without forming any liquid. This change is called
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through the liquid state.

questions.stem: Gases can be compressed easily but solids cannot, because the particles of a gas are
options: far apart with large spaces between them
questions.explanation: The large spaces between gas particles can be reduced by pressure, while solid particles are already close together.

questions.topic: Characteristics of living and non-living things
questions.stem: The ability of living things to respond to changes around them is called
questions.explanation: Living things detect and respond to stimuli such as light, touch and heat; this is irritability.

questions.topic: Characteristics of living and non-living things
questions.stem: Living things release energy from food by the process of
questions.explanation: In respiration, food is broken down, usually using oxygen, to release energy for life activities.

questions.topic: Characteristics of living and non-living things
questions.stem: A car moves and uses fuel, but it is a non-living thing because it cannot
questions.explanation: Cars move and use energy, but they cannot grow, reproduce or respond to stimuli as living things do.

questions.topic: Plants and animals: examples, characteristics and importance
questions.stem: Animals that have a backbone are called
questions.explanation: Vertebrates such as fish, frogs, lizards, birds and mammals have a backbone.

questions.topic: Plants and animals: examples, characteristics and importance
questions.stem: Plants are important to animals mainly because they
options: produce carbon dioxide for animals to breathe
questions.explanation: Plants make food by photosynthesis and release oxygen, which animals need to live.

questions.topic: Plants and animals: examples, characteristics and importance
questions.stem: Which of the following is a flowering plant?
questions.explanation: Hibiscus produces flowers; mosses and ferns are non-flowering plants and the mushroom is a fungus.

questions.stem: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall outside the membrane; both plant and animal cells have a membrane, nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.stem: Growth in plants differs from growth in most animals because plants
options: continue to grow throughout life at the tips of roots and shoots
stop growing as soon as they are born
questions.explanation: Plants have growing regions at their tips that remain active throughout life, while most animals stop growing at adulthood.

questions.topic: Examples, properties, uses and importance of living and non-living things
questions.stem: Air is important to living things mainly because it contains
questions.explanation: Living things use the oxygen in air to release energy from food.

questions.topic: Examples, properties, uses and importance of living and non-living things
questions.stem: Water is used to cool car engines mainly because it
options: can absorb a large amount of heat
is a good conductor of electricity
questions.explanation: Water absorbs much heat for a small rise in temperature, so it carries heat away from the engine.

questions.topic: Classification of non-living things into metals and non-metals
questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a yellow, brittle, non-conducting element; copper, iron and aluminium are metals.

questions.topic: Classification of non-living things into metals and non-metals
questions.stem: Copper is used for making electrical wires mainly because it
options: is a good conductor of electricity
questions.explanation: Copper allows electric current to flow easily and can be drawn into wires.

questions.topic: Classification of non-living things into metals and non-metals
questions.stem: Non-metals are generally
options: shiny and easily hammered into sheets
poor conductors of heat and electricity and brittle when solid
questions.explanation: Most non-metals, such as sulphur, are dull, brittle and do not conduct; graphite is an exception.

questions.topic: Classification of non-living things into metals and non-metals
questions.stem: Mercury is unusual among metals because it is
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only common metal that is liquid at room temperature, which is why it is used in some thermometers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a terrestrial habitat?
questions.explanation: Terrestrial habitats are on land; rivers, lagoons and the sea are aquatic habitats.

questions.stem: An example of a marine habitat is the
questions.explanation: Marine habitats are salt-water habitats such as the sea and the ocean.

questions.stem: An animal that lives mainly in trees, such as a monkey, is described as
questions.explanation: Arboreal animals live in trees and have adaptations such as gripping hands or tails.

questions.topic: Adaptation of living things to their habitat
questions.stem: Ducks have webbed feet that help them to
questions.explanation: Webbed feet act like paddles, pushing against water as the duck swims.

questions.topic: Adaptation of living things to their habitat
questions.stem: A camel is able to survive in the desert mainly because it
options: can go for long periods without water and has broad feet for walking on sand
questions.explanation: The camel conserves water and its broad feet stop it from sinking into the sand.

questions.topic: Adaptation of living things to their habitat
questions.stem: Birds have hollow bones. This adaptation helps them to
options: fly, because it makes the body light
questions.explanation: Hollow bones reduce body weight without much loss of strength, making flight easier.

questions.topic: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
questions.stem: A lion kills and eats an antelope. The lion is described as a
questions.explanation: A predator hunts and kills other animals (prey) for food.

questions.topic: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
questions.stem: Bees collect nectar from flowers and in turn help to pollinate them. This relationship, in which both benefit, is called
questions.explanation: In mutualism both organisms benefit: the bee gets food and the flower is pollinated.

questions.topic: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
questions.stem: Two goats struggling for the same small patch of grass are in
questions.explanation: Competition occurs when organisms need the same limited resource.

questions.topic: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
questions.stem: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals in the soil are called
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.topic: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
questions.stem: Cattle egrets follow grazing cattle and eat the insects disturbed by them, while the cattle are neither helped nor harmed. This relationship is
questions.explanation: In commensalism, one organism benefits and the other is not affected.

questions.stem: Using our senses to gather information about things around us is called
questions.explanation: Observation is gathering information through seeing, hearing, touching, smelling and tasting.

questions.stem: Drawing a conclusion from what has been observed is called
questions.explanation: An inference explains or interprets an observation; for example, wet ground suggests that it rained.

questions.stem: The strong desire of human beings to ask questions and find out how things work is called
questions.explanation: Inquisitiveness drives people to explore and discover, which leads to scientific knowledge.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure the weight of a person?
questions.explanation: A weighing scale measures body weight; a thermometer measures temperature.

questions.stem: The stage of development between childhood and adulthood is called
questions.explanation: Adolescence is the period of change from childhood into adulthood.

questions.stem: Growth in living things can be described as
options: a temporary swelling of the body
a permanent increase in size, height or weight
questions.explanation: Growth is an irreversible increase in size or mass of a living thing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a TEMPORARY change in the body?
options: Swelling caused by an insect bite
Breaking of the voice in boys
questions.explanation: Swelling from a bite goes down after some time; the other changes are permanent changes of development.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a chemical commonly used in the kitchen?
questions.explanation: Table salt is a chemical compound; chemicals are substances with a definite composition, natural or man-made.

questions.stem: Paracetamol tablets and cough syrup are examples of
questions.explanation: Pharmaceutical chemicals are used as medicines.

questions.stem: Uranium used to produce energy in nuclear power stations is an example of a
questions.explanation: Nuclear chemicals are radioactive substances used in nuclear reactors.

questions.stem: Sulphuric acid used in car batteries is an example of an
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid is produced in large amounts for industrial uses such as batteries and fertilizers.

questions.stem: Chemicals such as test reagents and indicators used in school science experiments are called
questions.explanation: Laboratory chemicals are used for tests and experiments in laboratories.

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as highly hazardous and toxic?
questions.explanation: Rat poison can kill humans and animals in small amounts, so it is highly hazardous and toxic.

questions.stem: A skull and crossbones symbol on a container means that the chemical is
questions.explanation: The skull and crossbones is the hazard symbol for toxic substances.

questions.stem: When handling corrosive chemicals in the laboratory, a student should wear
questions.explanation: Gloves and goggles protect the skin and eyes from burns by corrosive chemicals.

questions.stem: A container showing a flame symbol holds a substance that is
questions.explanation: The flame symbol warns that the substance, such as petrol or methylated spirit, burns easily.

questions.stem: Chemicals should NOT be stored in empty soft-drink bottles because
options: someone, especially a child, may drink them by mistake
the chemicals will turn into soft drinks
questions.explanation: Familiar drink bottles invite people to drink from them, which can cause poisoning.

questions.stem: If a chemical splashes into the eye, the first thing to do is to
options: rinse the eye with plenty of clean running water
apply palm oil to the eye
questions.explanation: Flushing with clean water quickly dilutes and removes the chemical before seeking medical help.

questions.stem: A corrosive symbol on a chemical container warns that the chemical can
options: destroy skin and other materials on contact
questions.explanation: Corrosive chemicals such as strong acids and alkalis eat away skin, metals and other materials.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a family trait that can be inherited?
questions.explanation: Albinism is passed from parents to children through genes; scars, injuries and tans are acquired, not inherited.

questions.stem: Characteristics passed from parents to their children are called
questions.explanation: Inherited traits are passed on through genes from parents to offspring.

questions.stem: Albinism is a condition in which the body
options: cannot produce enough of the skin pigment melanin
questions.explanation: People with albinism lack melanin, so their skin, hair and eyes are very light and the skin burns easily in the sun.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an acquired (learned) trait rather than an inherited one?
options: The ability to ride a bicycle
questions.explanation: Riding a bicycle is learned through practice; blood group, eye colour and dimples are inherited.

questions.stem: Which pair of traits are BOTH inherited?
options: Dimples and the ability to roll the tongue
Dimples and the ability to speak Hausa
questions.explanation: Dimples and tongue rolling are controlled by genes; language and scars are acquired.

questions.stem: A recessive trait is one that
options: shows only when the gene for it is received from both parents
questions.explanation: A recessive trait is hidden when a dominant gene is present, so it appears only when two recessive genes are inherited.

questions.stem: In a plant, the gene for tallness (T) is dominant over the gene for shortness (t). A plant with genotype Tt will be
questions.explanation: The dominant gene T shows its effect even when only one copy is present, so Tt plants are tall.

questions.stem: A pure tall plant (TT) is crossed with a pure short plant (tt). What fraction of the offspring will be tall?
questions.explanation: Every offspring receives T from one parent and t from the other, so all are Tt and tall.

questions.stem: Two parents with normal skin colour have a child with albinism. This shows that
options: both parents carry the recessive gene for albinism
albinism is caused by the sun
questions.explanation: A recessive trait can be hidden in parents who carry it; the child shows it after receiving the gene from both parents.

questions.stem: Children often resemble their parents because they
questions.explanation: Genes from both parents determine many features of the child, so children look like their parents.

questions.stem: Knowledge of family traits helps a person to trace his or her
questions.explanation: Shared traits and family records help people trace their ancestors and relationships.

questions.stem: Intelligence in a child is influenced by
questions.explanation: Genes give potential, but nutrition, education and home environment also affect how intelligence develops.

questions.stem: Which of the following causes soil erosion?
options: Removal of plant cover from the land
questions.explanation: Without plant cover, rain and wind easily wash or blow away the topsoil.

questions.stem: Large, deep channels cut into the land by running water, as seen in parts of Anambra State, are called
questions.explanation: Gully erosion forms deep channels when concentrated runoff cuts into soft soil.

questions.stem: Building step-like level platforms on hillsides to reduce soil erosion is called
questions.explanation: Terraces slow down runoff on slopes, so less soil is washed away.

questions.stem: The overflow of water onto land that is normally dry is called
questions.explanation: Flooding occurs when water covers land that is usually dry.

questions.stem: Which natural factor can cause flooding?
questions.explanation: When rain falls heavily for a long time, rivers and drains overflow.

questions.stem: Which measure helps to prevent flood damage in communities?
options: Avoiding building houses on river banks and flood plains
questions.explanation: Flood plains are natural overflow areas, so keeping buildings off them reduces flood damage.

questions.stem: One effect of flooding on farmland is that it
options: destroys crops and washes away fertile topsoil
questions.explanation: Flood water kills crops by waterlogging and carries away the fertile topsoil.

questions.stem: A drainage pattern in which small streams join a main river like the branches of a tree is called a
questions.explanation: Dendritic means tree-like; it is the most common drainage pattern.

questions.stem: Which practice commonly leads to bush burning in Nigeria?
options: Setting fire to bushes to drive out animals during hunting
questions.explanation: Hunters sometimes set bushes on fire to flush out animals, and the fire spreads widely.

questions.stem: An economic consequence of bush burning is the
options: destruction of crops, farm produce and property, causing loss of income
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled fires burn farms, barns and houses, so families lose food and money.

questions.stem: A cleared strip of land around a farm or forest reserve that stops fire from spreading is called a
questions.explanation: A firebreak has no dry vegetation to burn, so a bush fire cannot cross it.

questions.stem: Which is a domestic reason for cutting down trees in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Many households depend on firewood for cooking, which leads to the cutting of trees.

questions.stem: Cutting down trees to sell as timber to furniture makers is a
questions.explanation: Logging for sale is a commercial reason for deforestation.

questions.stem: One effect of deforestation on the environment is the
options: loss of habitats for wild animals
questions.explanation: Forests are homes for many animals, so clearing them destroys their habitats.

questions.stem: To control deforestation, regulations in Nigeria require loggers to
options: cut trees in forest reserves freely
questions.explanation: Permits limit the number of trees cut, and replanting replaces trees that are removed.

questions.stem: Desertification is the
options: planting of trees in the desert
spread of desert-like conditions into land that was once fertile
questions.explanation: In desertification, land becomes dry and barren like a desert.

questions.stem: Which human activity is a cause of desertification?
questions.explanation: When too many animals graze an area, the plant cover is removed and the soil becomes bare and dry.

questions.stem: Which measure helps to control desertification?
options: Controlled grazing and planting of trees
Keeping more livestock than the land can support
questions.explanation: Limiting grazing and planting trees protect and restore the plant cover.

questions.topic: Depletion of the ozone layer and its effects
questions.stem: The ozone layer is found in the part of the atmosphere called the
questions.explanation: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, about 15 to 35 km above the earth.

questions.topic: Depletion of the ozone layer and its effects
questions.stem: The warming of the earth when gases such as carbon dioxide trap heat in the atmosphere is called the
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases let sunlight in but trap heat, warming the earth.

questions.topic: Depletion of the ozone layer and its effects
questions.stem: Ozone is a form of
options: oxygen with three atoms in each molecule
questions.explanation: Ozone (O3) is made of three oxygen atoms, while ordinary oxygen (O2) has two.

questions.topic: Depletion of the ozone layer and its effects
questions.stem: Global warming can lead to flooding of coastal cities such as Lagos mainly because
options: melting ice causes sea levels to rise
questions.explanation: Higher temperatures melt ice in polar regions, and the extra water raises sea levels.

questions.stem: Old refrigerators and air conditioners should be disposed of properly mainly because they may release
options: chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) that damage the ozone layer
questions.explanation: CFCs from old cooling equipment rise into the stratosphere and destroy ozone.

questions.stem: Which household practice helps to reduce harmful gases released into the atmosphere?
options: Using cleaner cooking fuels instead of burning refuse and firewood
questions.explanation: Cleaner fuels and less burning reduce smoke and gases released into the air.

questions.stem: Strong pain-relieving tablets such as tramadol should be taken only
options: in double doses for faster relief
with a doctor's prescription and in the stated dose
questions.explanation: Tramadol is a controlled drug; taking it without prescription or in large doses leads to addiction, seizures and even death.

questions.stem: Which is a possible effect of drug abuse on the body?
questions.explanation: Drug abuse can irritate the stomach, cause skin reactions and harm many organs.

questions.stem: Sniffing glue or petrol can damage the
questions.explanation: Inhaled fumes injure the lining of the nose and lungs and harm the brain.

questions.stem: Sharing needles to inject drugs can cause
options: injection abscesses and infections such as HIV and hepatitis
questions.explanation: Dirty needles carry germs into the body, causing abscesses and blood-borne infections.

questions.stem: Addiction to a drug means that the person
options: has a strong dependence on it and cannot stop without help
takes the drug only as prescribed
questions.explanation: An addicted person craves the drug and suffers withdrawal symptoms when it is stopped.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a healthy way of coping with stress?
options: Talking to a trusted adult and taking regular exercise
questions.explanation: Sharing problems and staying active reduce stress without harming the body.

questions.stem: Taking part in sports and school clubs helps to prevent drug abuse mainly by
options: keeping young people busy with healthy activities and good friends
questions.explanation: Positive activities and good company build confidence and reduce idleness and bad influences.

questions.topic: Activities of drug control agencies (NAFDAC, NDLEA)
questions.stem: Which of the following is an activity of NAFDAC?
options: Seizing and destroying fake and expired drugs
questions.explanation: NAFDAC removes fake, expired and unregistered drugs and foods from the market and destroys them.

questions.topic: Activities of drug control agencies (NAFDAC, NDLEA)
questions.stem: NDLEA officers locate and destroy farms where cannabis is grown illegally in order to
options: reduce the supply of illegal drugs
questions.explanation: Destroying cannabis farms cuts off the supply of the drug.

questions.topic: Activities of drug control agencies (NAFDAC, NDLEA)
questions.stem: Apart from arresting drug dealers, the NDLEA also
options: carries out drug education, counselling and rehabilitation of drug users
questions.explanation: NDLEA runs awareness campaigns and helps drug users to recover, in addition to enforcing the law.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a misuse of herbal medicine?
options: Taking herbal mixtures in unknown doses for every illness
questions.explanation: Unknown doses can cause poisoning or damage to organs, so taking herbs this way is misuse.

questions.stem: Taking a herbal mixture together with medicines prescribed by a doctor can be dangerous because
options: they may react with each other and cause harmful effects
questions.explanation: Herbs contain active chemicals that can strengthen, weaken or change the effect of prescribed drugs.

questions.stem: Crops grown mainly for sale, such as cocoa and rubber, are called
questions.explanation: Cash crops are grown mainly for sale to earn money rather than for home use.

questions.stem: Henna (lalle) and indigo are plant resources used mainly as
questions.explanation: Henna and indigo give colour to the skin, hair and cloth, so they are plant dyes.

questions.stem: Shea butter, obtained from the nuts of the shea tree, is used mainly in
questions.explanation: Shea butter is used in creams, soaps and pomades and also as a cooking fat.

questions.stem: The anti-malarial drug quinine was first obtained from the bark of the
questions.explanation: Quinine is a natural drug from cinchona bark, showing that plants are sources of medicines.

questions.stem: Honey is a resource obtained from
questions.explanation: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.

questions.stem: Milk, cheese and yoghurt are called
questions.explanation: Dairy products are made from the milk of animals such as cows and goats.

questions.stem: Hides and skins of cattle and goats are processed to make
options: leather for shoes, bags and drums
questions.explanation: Hides and skins are tanned into leather, which is used for many products.

questions.topic: Economic importance of resources from living things
questions.stem: The leather and textile industries in Kano, which use hides and cotton, are important because they
options: provide employment and income for many people
questions.explanation: Industries that process resources from living things create jobs and income for individuals and society.

questions.topic: Economic importance of resources from living things
questions.stem: Which of the following BEST shows the economic importance of resources from living things to a country?
options: They have no use outside the home
They supply raw materials to industries and earn foreign exchange through exports
questions.explanation: Crops and animal products feed industries and are exported for foreign exchange, helping the economy.

questions.stem: Tin is mined mainly around
questions.explanation: Plateau State, especially around Jos, is Nigeria's main tin-mining area.

questions.stem: Limestone is used mainly for making
questions.explanation: Limestone is heated with clay to produce cement.

questions.stem: Clay is a non-living resource used for making
questions.explanation: Clay can be shaped when wet and hardened by firing, so it is used for pottery and bricks.

questions.stem: Sand is a non-living resource used mainly for
questions.explanation: Sand is mixed with cement for building and is the main raw material for glass.

questions.stem: Ewekoro in Ogun State is well known for
questions.explanation: Ewekoro has large limestone deposits used by cement factories.

questions.stem: Gypsum, a solid mineral, is used in making
questions.explanation: Gypsum is used to make plaster of Paris (POP) for ceilings and is added to cement.

questions.stem: Granite rocks are quarried in Nigeria mainly for
questions.explanation: Crushed granite (chippings) is used in concrete and road building.

questions.stem: Mining of solid minerals benefits Nigeria by
options: providing jobs, raw materials and government revenue
questions.explanation: Solid minerals supply industries, create jobs and earn revenue and foreign exchange.

questions.stem: Iron ore is mined at Itakpe in
questions.explanation: Itakpe in Kogi State has iron ore deposits that supply the Ajaokuta steel project.

questions.stem: Large deposits of gold are found in
questions.explanation: Gold is mined in places such as Zamfara and around Ilesha in Osun State.

questions.stem: Bitumen (tar sand) deposits in Nigeria are found mainly in
questions.explanation: Nigeria's large bitumen deposits lie in a belt across Ondo and neighbouring states in the south-west.

questions.stem: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed but
options: can only be stored in food
can be changed from one form to another
can only be produced by the sun
questions.explanation: Energy is never lost; it only changes form, for example from chemical energy in fuel to heat.

questions.stem: The energy possessed by a body because of its motion is called
questions.explanation: Any moving object, such as a rolling ball or a moving car, has kinetic energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of energy for the human body?
questions.explanation: Food contains chemical energy that the body releases during respiration.

questions.stem: Firewood, charcoal and animal dung burnt for cooking are examples of
questions.explanation: Biomass energy comes from plant and animal materials.

questions.stem: Wind can be used as a source of energy to
options: turn wind turbines that generate electricity
questions.explanation: The moving air turns the blades of a wind turbine, which drives a generator.

questions.stem: The form of energy that we can hear is
questions.explanation: Sound energy is carried by vibrations that our ears detect.

questions.stem: The energy stored in food and in batteries is
questions.explanation: Food and batteries store energy in chemical substances, released by chemical reactions.

questions.stem: Energy released from the nucleus of atoms in a nuclear power station is called
questions.explanation: Nuclear energy comes from splitting (or joining) the nuclei of atoms.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 2 kg is moving with a velocity of 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = ½mv² = ½ x 2 x 3 x 3 = 9 J.

questions.stem: An electric fan changes electrical energy mainly into
questions.explanation: The motor of the fan uses electrical energy to turn the blades.

questions.stem: An electric pressing iron changes electrical energy mainly into
questions.explanation: The heating element of the iron gets hot when current passes through it.

questions.stem: During photosynthesis, green plants change light energy into
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight to make sugars, which store chemical energy.

questions.stem: When you rub your palms together quickly, they become warm. This shows the change of
questions.explanation: Friction from the moving hands turns kinetic energy into heat.

questions.stem: In a petrol generator, the correct order of energy changes is
options: electrical energy to chemical energy to heat energy
chemical energy to mechanical energy to electrical energy
mechanical energy to chemical energy to light energy
light energy to sound energy to chemical energy
questions.explanation: Burning petrol (chemical energy) drives the engine (mechanical energy), which turns the generator to produce electricity.

questions.stem: Hospitals need a steady supply of electrical energy mainly to
options: power equipment and keep vaccines and blood cold
questions.explanation: Electricity runs medical machines, lighting and refrigerators that store vaccines and blood.

questions.topic: Meaning of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Non-renewable sources of energy are those that
options: cannot be replaced once they are used up
are replaced every day by nature
questions.explanation: Non-renewable sources such as coal, crude oil and natural gas take millions of years to form.

questions.topic: Meaning of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Fossil fuels such as coal and crude oil were formed from
options: the remains of plants and animals buried for millions of years
questions.explanation: Heat and pressure slowly changed buried remains of living things into fossil fuels.

questions.topic: Examples of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Wind is continually produced by the sun's heating of the atmosphere, so it does not run out.

questions.topic: Examples of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Solar panels on rooftops change
questions.explanation: Solar cells in the panels convert light energy directly into electricity.

questions.topic: Examples of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Natural gas used for cooking is classified as
questions.explanation: Natural gas is a fossil fuel and cannot be replaced once used up.

questions.topic: Examples of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Biogas, produced from decaying animal dung and food waste, is a renewable source of energy because
options: it takes millions of years to form
the waste materials are produced continually
it is found only in deep rocks
questions.explanation: Animals and households keep producing waste, so biogas can be made again and again.

questions.topic: Use and misuse of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Flaring of natural gas at oil fields in the Niger Delta is a misuse of energy because it
options: wastes a useful fuel and pollutes the air
questions.explanation: Burning off gas wastes energy that could be used and releases smoke and greenhouse gases.

questions.topic: Use and misuse of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Running a petrol generator inside a closed room is dangerous mainly because it can cause
questions.explanation: Generator exhaust contains carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas that can kill people in closed spaces.

questions.topic: Use and misuse of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem: Energy-saving LED bulbs save electricity mainly because they
options: change more of the electrical energy into light and less into heat
questions.explanation: LED bulbs waste less energy as heat, so they give the same light with less electricity.

questions.stem: A steady supply of electricity helps a society mainly by
options: supporting industries, creating jobs and improving living standards
questions.explanation: Industries, hospitals, schools and businesses depend on energy, so reliable power improves life and the economy.

questions.stem: Nigeria should develop more renewable sources of energy mainly because
options: renewable sources are always free of cost
the sun will stop shining soon
fossil fuels will eventually run out and they pollute the environment
questions.explanation: Renewable sources are sustainable and cleaner, reducing dependence on fuels that are running out.

questions.stem: The instrument used to measure the weight of a body is the
questions.explanation: A spring balance measures force, so it is used to measure weight in newtons.

questions.stem: The weight of a body is the
options: force with which gravity pulls it
questions.explanation: Weight is the pull of gravity on a body and is measured in newtons; mass is the amount of matter.

questions.stem: Compared with its mass on earth, the mass of a stone taken to the moon is
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in the stone, which does not change from place to place; only weight changes.

questions.stem: The force of gravity on the moon is about one-sixth of that on earth. A man weighs 600 N on earth. What will he weigh on the moon?
questions.explanation: Weight on the moon = 600 N / 6 = 100 N.

questions.stem: Day and night are caused by the
options: rotation of the earth on its axis
movement of the moon around the earth
questions.explanation: As the earth spins, the side facing the sun has day and the other side has night.

questions.stem: The sun is a
questions.explanation: The sun is a star, a huge ball of hot gases that gives out its own light and heat.

questions.stem: Which planet is closest to the sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the innermost planet of the solar system.

questions.stem: The earth rotates once on its axis in about
questions.explanation: One complete rotation takes about 24 hours, giving one day and night.

questions.stem: The largest planet in the solar system is
questions.explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant and the biggest planet.

questions.stem: How many planets are there in the solar system?
questions.explanation: The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

questions.stem: The seasons of the year are caused by the
options: daily rotation of the earth only
tilt of the earth's axis as the earth revolves round the sun
questions.explanation: Because the axis is tilted, different parts of the earth receive more or less direct sunlight at different times of the year.

questions.stem: A person trained to travel into space is called an
questions.explanation: Astronauts travel and work in spacecraft; astronomers study objects in space.

questions.stem: Satellites are carried from the earth into space by
questions.explanation: Only rockets are powerful enough to lift satellites into orbit.

questions.stem: The Nigerian government agency responsible for space research and satellite development is
questions.explanation: The National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA) manages Nigeria's satellite programme.

questions.stem: Satellites used for the Global Positioning System (GPS) help people to
questions.explanation: GPS satellites send signals that devices use to work out their exact position.

questions.stem: Nigeria's first satellite, NigeriaSat-1, was launched in
questions.explanation: NigeriaSat-1, an earth observation satellite, was launched in 2003.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a radioactive element?
questions.explanation: Uranium has unstable atoms that give out radiation, so it is radioactive.

questions.stem: Radiation from radioactive substances is used in hospitals to
questions.explanation: Controlled radiation can destroy cancer cells.

questions.stem: Exposure to large amounts of radiation can cause
questions.explanation: High doses of radiation damage body cells and can cause burns, sickness and cancer.

questions.stem: Crude oil is also called
questions.explanation: Crude oil, as it comes out of the ground, is called petroleum.

questions.stem: Nigeria's crude oil refineries are located at
questions.explanation: The state-owned refineries are at Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna.

questions.stem: In the fractional distillation of crude oil, the fractions are separated because they have different
questions.explanation: Each fraction condenses at a different temperature in the column, according to its boiling point.

questions.stem: The fraction of crude oil with the lowest boiling point, which collects at the top of the column, is
questions.explanation: Gases have the lowest boiling points, so they rise to the top of the column.

questions.topic: Uses of crude oil and petrochemicals
questions.stem: Diesel obtained from crude oil is used mainly to
options: run lorries, buses and large generators
questions.explanation: Diesel is the fuel for diesel engines in lorries, buses and generators.

questions.topic: Uses of crude oil and petrochemicals
questions.stem: Lubricating oil from crude oil is used in engines to
questions.explanation: Lubricants form a thin layer between parts so they move smoothly and wear less.

questions.topic: Uses of crude oil and petrochemicals
questions.stem: Which of the following is a petrochemical product?
questions.explanation: Plastics are made from chemicals obtained from crude oil and natural gas.

questions.topic: Importance of crude oil and petrochemicals
questions.stem: Crude oil is important to Nigerian industry mainly because it
options: provides raw materials for petrochemical industries and creates jobs
questions.explanation: Petrochemical industries use crude oil products to make plastics, fertilizers and detergents, providing employment.

questions.topic: Importance of crude oil and petrochemicals
questions.stem: Illegal refining of crude oil in creeks of the Niger Delta is dangerous mainly because it
options: causes fires, deaths and serious pollution of land and water
questions.explanation: Crude methods of boiling oil cause explosions and spill wastes that destroy farmland, rivers and health.

questions.stem: Learning a trade by working under a master craftsman for some years is called
questions.explanation: In an apprenticeship, a learner gains a skill through practical training under an experienced person.

questions.stem: Taking, processing and printing pictures for a living requires
questions.explanation: Photography is a skill that can be learned and used to earn income.

questions.stem: Using a computer to type documents and send e-mails is an example of
questions.explanation: Basic computer literacy is the ability to use a computer for simple everyday tasks.

questions.stem: Learning how to raise poultry and grow vegetables is an example of a
questions.explanation: Farming skills involve producing crops and animals.

questions.stem: Learning first aid is useful mainly for
questions.explanation: First aid skills help a person to give immediate help when accidents or emergencies happen.

questions.stem: Skills serve as a survival strategy mainly because a skilled person can
options: earn a living even in difficult times
questions.explanation: A useful skill allows a person to find work or create a job when other opportunities are scarce.

questions.stem: Working together with classmates on a craft project helps students to
options: learn to cooperate and live together
questions.explanation: Group skill activities teach teamwork, sharing and respect for others.

questions.stem: A young tailor uses her savings to open a shop, not knowing whether customers will come. This shows that skill acquisition involves
questions.explanation: Starting a business with a new skill means taking a calculated risk in the hope of success.

questions.stem: Skill acquisition improves a person's quality of life mainly because it
options: reduces the person's chances of work
questions.explanation: A skilled person earns more, can meet needs and feels confident about his or her abilities.

questions.topic: Right and wrong application of science
questions.stem: Which of the following is a RIGHT application of science?
options: Using chemicals to kill fish in rivers
questions.explanation: Vaccines protect people's health, which is a good use of scientific knowledge.

questions.topic: Right and wrong application of science
questions.stem: Scientists are expected to
options: be honest and follow ethical rules in their work
hide harmful effects of their products
questions.explanation: Ethics require honesty and care so that science benefits people and does not harm them.

questions.topic: Right and wrong application of science
questions.stem: Using nuclear knowledge to make weapons that can destroy whole cities is an example of
questions.explanation: Science used to cause mass destruction is a wrong application.

questions.stem: Spraying vegetables with too much pesticide just before selling them can
options: poison the people who eat them
reduce the cost of production for buyers
questions.explanation: Pesticide residues on food can cause poisoning and long-term illness.

questions.stem: Dumping old computers and phones carelessly can pollute the environment because they contain
options: harmful metals such as lead and mercury
questions.explanation: Electronic waste contains toxic metals that leak into soil and water.

questions.stem: Using antibiotics carelessly in poultry feed to make birds grow faster can lead to
questions.explanation: Overuse allows resistant bacteria to survive and spread, making infections harder to treat.

questions.stem: Changing the results of a scientific experiment to get a desired answer is dangerous mainly because it
options: leads to wrong conclusions that can harm people
questions.explanation: Falsified results lead to unsafe products and decisions based on false information.

questions.topic: Adverse effects of bad scientific practices on a country
questions.stem: The collapse of buildings constructed with substandard materials leads to
questions.explanation: Ignoring standards in building causes collapses that kill people and destroy property.

questions.topic: Adverse effects of bad scientific practices on a country
questions.stem: When a country's exported farm produce is rejected abroad because it contains too much pesticide, the country
options: loses foreign exchange and its reputation in trade
questions.explanation: Rejection of exports cuts earnings and makes foreign buyers distrust products from that country.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a balanced diet? [2 marks]
(b) Name four classes of food nutrients and give ONE Nigerian food rich in each. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A diet that contains all the food nutrients in the right proportions for the needs of the body
1 mark: (b) Carbohydrate
1 mark: (b) e.g. yam, rice, garri, bread
1 mark: (b) Protein
1 mark: (b) e.g. beans, fish, egg, meat
1 mark: (b) Fats and oils
1 mark: (b) e.g. palm oil, groundnut oil, butter
1 mark: (b) Vitamins or minerals (or water)
1 mark: (b) e.g. oranges, vegetables, milk
questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies every nutrient the body needs. Each class of nutrient is found in common Nigerian foods.

questions.topic: Causes of air, soil and water pollution
questions.stem:
(a) Define water pollution. [2 marks]
(b) State two causes each of air pollution and soil pollution. [4 marks]
(c) State four ways of controlling pollution. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Water pollution is the addition of harmful substances to water, making it unsafe for living things
1 mark: (b) Air: smoke from vehicles, generators or factories
1 mark: (b) Air: burning refuse, bush burning or gas flaring
1 mark: (b) Soil: oil spillage or excess fertilizers/pesticides
1 mark: (b) Soil: dumping non-biodegradable materials such as polythene and industrial waste
1 mark: (c) Proper refuse disposal (landfill, recycling)
1 mark: (c) Treating industrial waste and sewage before discharge
1 mark: (c) Servicing vehicles and generators / reducing burning
1 mark: (c) Enforcing environmental laws (e.g. NESREA) / careful use of agricultural chemicals
questions.explanation: Pollution of air, soil and water comes from human activities, and it is controlled by good waste disposal, treatment of waste and enforcement of laws.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three states of matter and give ONE example of each. [6 marks]
(b) Name the change of state that takes place when: (i) ice turns to water (ii) water turns to steam (iii) steam turns to water (iv) camphor turns directly to vapour. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Solid
1 mark: (a) e.g. stone, ice, wood
1 mark: (a) Liquid
1 mark: (a) e.g. water, kerosene, palm oil
1 mark: (a) Gas
1 mark: (a) e.g. oxygen, air, steam
1 mark: (b)(i) Melting
1 mark: (b)(ii) Boiling (evaporation)
1 mark: (b)(iii) Condensation
1 mark: (b)(iv) Sublimation
questions.explanation: Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases and changes state when heated or cooled.

questions.topic: Characteristics of living and non-living things
questions.stem:
(a) State five characteristics of living things. [5 marks]
(b) State three differences between plants and animals. [3 marks]
(c) Give two examples of non-living things. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Movement
1 mark: (a) Respiration
1 mark: (a) Nutrition (feeding)
1 mark: (a) Growth
1 mark: (a) Reproduction (accept excretion, irritability)
1 mark: (b) Plants make their own food by photosynthesis; animals feed on ready-made food
1 mark: (b) Plants are mostly fixed in one place; animals move about
1 mark: (b) Plant cells have cell walls and chlorophyll; animal cells do not
1 mark: (c) e.g. stone
1 mark: (c) e.g. table, water, car
questions.explanation: Living things share characteristics such as feeding, respiring, growing and reproducing. Plants and animals differ in feeding, movement and cell structure.

questions.topic: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
questions.stem:
(a) What is a habitat? Give ONE example of an aquatic and ONE example of a terrestrial habitat. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the following relationships with ONE example each: (i) predation (ii) mutualism (iii) parasitism. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A habitat is the natural home of an organism, where it lives and gets food
1 mark: (a) Aquatic: pond, river, lagoon or sea
1 mark: (a) Terrestrial: forest, grassland or desert
1 mark: (b)(i) Predation: one animal kills and eats another
1 mark: (b)(i) e.g. hawk and chick, lion and antelope
1 mark: (b)(ii) Mutualism: both organisms benefit
1 mark: (b)(ii) e.g. bee and flower
1 mark: (b)(iii) Parasitism: one organism lives on or in another and harms it
1 mark: (b)(iii) e.g. tick on a dog, tapeworm in man
questions.explanation: Organisms in a habitat interact in different ways; in some relationships both gain, in others one gains at the other's expense.

questions.stem:
(a) Classify chemicals according to their uses, giving ONE example of each class. [6 marks]
(b) State four safety measures to observe when storing or using chemicals at home or in the laboratory. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Pharmaceutical/cosmetic chemicals
1 mark: (a) e.g. paracetamol, body cream
1 mark: (a) Industrial chemicals
1 mark: (a) e.g. sulphuric acid, caustic soda
1 mark: (a) Laboratory (or nuclear) chemicals
1 mark: (a) e.g. indicators, test reagents (or uranium)
1 mark: (b) Read and follow the manufacturer's instructions on the label
1 mark: (b) Store in properly labelled containers
1 mark: (b) Keep out of reach of children, away from food
1 mark: (b) Wear protective clothing such as gloves and goggles / never taste chemicals
questions.explanation: Chemicals are grouped by use, and safe storage and handling prevent poisoning, burns and fires.

questions.stem:
In a plant, the gene for red flowers (R) is dominant over the gene for white flowers (r).
(a) Explain the terms dominant trait and recessive trait. [4 marks]
(b) A pure red-flowered plant (RR) is crossed with a white-flowered plant (rr). Show the cross and state the colour of the offspring. [4 marks]
(c) Two of the offspring from (b) are crossed. Show the cross and state the ratio of red to white flowers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Dominant trait: a trait that shows even when only one gene for it is present
2 marks: (a) Recessive trait: a trait that shows only when two genes for it are present (it is hidden by the dominant gene)
2 marks: (b) Gametes R and r; all offspring are Rr
2 marks: (b) All offspring have red flowers
2 marks: (c) Rr x Rr gives RR, Rr, Rr, rr
2 marks: (c) Ratio 3 red : 1 white
questions.explanation: A dominant gene masks a recessive one. Crossing RR with rr gives all Rr (red); crossing Rr with Rr gives 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr, which is 3 red to 1 white.

questions.stem:
(a) What is soil erosion? [2 marks]
(b) State four causes of soil erosion. [4 marks]
(c) State four ways of controlling soil erosion. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Soil erosion is the removal of the topsoil from one place to another by agents such as water and wind
1 mark: (b) Deforestation / removal of plant cover
1 mark: (b) Overgrazing
1 mark: (b) Bush burning
1 mark: (b) Heavy rainfall, poor farming on slopes or blocked drainage
1 mark: (c) Planting trees and cover crops
1 mark: (c) Terracing or contour ridging on slopes
1 mark: (c) Mulching
1 mark: (c) Building good drainage channels / controlled grazing
questions.explanation: Erosion happens when soil is left bare and exposed to rain and wind. Keeping the soil covered and slowing runoff control it.

questions.topic: Activities of drug control agencies (NAFDAC, NDLEA)
questions.stem:
(a) State four effects of drug abuse on the body. [4 marks]
(b) State two activities each of NAFDAC and NDLEA. [4 marks]
(c) Suggest two ways young people can avoid drug abuse. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Damage to the brain, mental illness or poor concentration
1 mark: (a) Damage to the lungs and nostrils (from sniffing or smoking)
1 mark: (a) Stomach upset, liver or kidney damage
1 mark: (a) Skin rashes, injection abscesses or HIV/hepatitis from shared needles
1 mark: (b) NAFDAC: registers and controls the quality of foods, drugs and cosmetics
1 mark: (b) NAFDAC: seizes and destroys fake and expired products
1 mark: (b) NDLEA: arrests and prosecutes drug traffickers and destroys illegal drug farms
1 mark: (b) NDLEA: carries out drug education, counselling and rehabilitation
1 mark: (c) Saying no to peer pressure / keeping good friends
1 mark: (c) Engaging in sports, clubs and other healthy activities / seeking help from trusted adults
questions.explanation: Drug abuse damages many organs. NAFDAC regulates products while NDLEA fights illegal drugs, and healthy lifestyles help young people avoid drugs.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four solid minerals found in Nigeria and state where each is found. [8 marks]
(b) State two economic importance of solid minerals to Nigeria. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Coal
1 mark: (a) Enugu

questions.stem:
(a) Name four forms of energy. [4 marks]
(b) State the main energy change that takes place in each of the following: (i) a torch battery in use (ii) an electric bulb (iii) a car engine. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:

1 mark: (a) Light energy
1 mark: (a) Sound energy

2 marks: (b)(ii) Electrical energy to light (and heat) energy

questions.topic: Examples of renewable and non-renewable energy
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable energy. [4 marks]
(b) Give three examples of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Renewable energy comes from sources that are naturally replaced and will not run out
2 marks: (a) Non-renewable energy comes from sources that cannot be replaced once used up
1 mark: (b) Renewable: solar
1 mark: (b) Renewable: wind
1 mark: (b) Renewable: hydro (water), biomass or biogas
1 mark: (b) Non-renewable: coal
1 mark: (b) Non-renewable: crude oil (petrol, diesel, kerosene)
1 mark: (b) Non-renewable: natural gas or nuclear fuel
questions.explanation: Renewable sources such as sun and wind are replaced naturally; fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas are not.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the eight planets of the solar system in order from the sun. [4 marks]
(b) Explain how day and night occur. [4 marks]
(c) State four uses of artificial satellites. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars
2 marks: (a) Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
2 marks: (b) The earth rotates (spins) on its axis once in about 24 hours
2 marks: (b) The side facing the sun has day while the side away from the sun has night
1 mark: (c) Telecommunication (telephone, television)
1 mark: (c) Weather forecasting
1 mark: (c) Navigation (GPS)
1 mark: (c) Mapping, earth observation or security monitoring

questions.stem:
(a) Name the process used in refining crude oil and explain how it separates the fractions. [4 marks]
(b) Name four products of crude oil and give ONE use of each. [8 marks]

2 marks: (a) Fractional distillation
2 marks: (a) Crude oil is heated; the vapours rise up the column and condense at different levels according to their boiling points
1 mark: (b) Petroleum gas
1 mark: (b) Cooking (LPG)
1 mark: (b) Petrol
1 mark: (b) Fuel for cars

1 mark: (b) Lubricating oil or bitumen
